our_argument_summary: WIN-043 claims a 2.26× longitudinal:latitudinal NMP drift ratio. Our detail_evidence shows it is post-hoc arithmetic from public NOAA NP.xy data with no dome derivation; detail_verdict_text carries the three-counter defender pivot rebuttal (verifiability ≠ derivation; W019 self-contradiction with time-window preempt now folded in; structural impossibility from axially-symmetric H(r)); detail_extra carries the W019 5.5× contrast, the Axial Symmetry Paradox cross-ref, and the PRED-R004 forward-falsification flag. Post c5 patches: "both labeled as confirmation" replaced with "both presented as supportive of the dome's NMP narrative"; time-window preempt clause folded into counter (2) with multi-window data points; Livermore et al. 2020 added as co-citation alongside Chulliat. All three c5 holes_found are closed in the current text.

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: monitor.py has no entry for the 2.26× ratio (code_analysis.monitoring="none"). The 2.26× lives only in homepage prose. monitor.py fetches NOAA NP.xy and reports a total drift speed via empirical exponential fit; it never decomposes velocity into longitudinal/latitudinal components and never computes their ratio.
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: No code computes 2.26×. It is a static homepage assertion; the monitoring suite has no infrastructure to test it. Confirmed in monitor/analyst/globe-fingerprints/WIN-043.json (c3 audit) and unchanged in current repo.
data_sources_used: https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/geomag/data/poles/NP.xy (NOAA NGDC pole position 1590-2025, 436 rows fetched this cycle; the dome itself cites this dataset)
dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: No canonical-window methodology is published. The dome silently equivocates between W019 (weekly observation, 5.5× lateral) and WIN-043 (unspecified multi-decade window, claimed 2.26×). The c6 fresh fetch confirms the unspecified-window degree of freedom: same NOAA dataset yields 1.69× over 1900-2025, 2.16× over 1990-2025, 2.70× over 2000-2025, 9.43× over 2010-2025, 2.34× over 2020-2025, 1.56× over 2024-2025. None of these is precisely 2.26×.
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: None. The c5 statements about monitor.py having no decomposition into directional components and no 2.26× literal all check out against the current code base.

code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: NOAA NP.xy spans 1590-2025 and predates the dome model by decades. The dome did not pre-register 2.26× before the trajectory was published; it adopted the value from existing data. monitor.py has no entry for this ratio so even the weak commit-timestamp test is inapplicable. detail_verdict_text correctly invokes Part 3.1b legitimate-novelty carve-out.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: No formula on the dome site derives 2.26× from any dome parameter (disc_radius, firmament_height, sun_altitude, moon_altitude). The dome's published field equations — H(r) = 8,537·exp(-r/8,619) and the two-pole sum B(r) = 62,376·exp(-r_N/8,619) + 64,852·exp(-r_S/8,619) (sections.json:part2 §2.10) — depend only on radial distances and cannot generate longitude-dependent quantities of any magnitude.

holes_found.description: Counter (3) and detail_extra 'Structural impossibility' both cite ONLY the H(r) altitude equation, not the two-pole B(r) sum (B(r) = 62,376·exp(-r_N/8,619) + 64,852·exp(-r_S/8,619)) which the dome also publishes for field-strength. §2.10 (Axial Symmetry Paradox) explicitly handles BOTH equations and shows the sum is bounded to at-most-dipolar east-west structure (the dual-lobe test), but the cross-ref is hidden behind 'see The Axial Symmetry Paradox.' A dome defender reading WIN-043 in isolation sees 'H(r) only' and pivots: 'we're not claiming 2.26× comes from H(r); aetheric vortex dynamics or the two-pole B(r) sum could in principle be longitude-dependent.' This was flagged in the c5 advocate_mode preemptive_recommendation but never filed as an ISS, so it persists. Surfacing B(r) inline in counter (3) closes the pivot without requiring the reader to follow the cross-ref.
holes_found.recommendation: Amend counter (3) to: 'The dome's published field equations all depend only on radial distance — H(r) = 8,537·exp(−r/8,619) (firmament height) and the two-pole sum B(r) = 62,376·exp(−r_N/8,619) + 64,852·exp(−r_S/8,619) (field strength) — neither can generate longitude-dependent quantities of any magnitude (see The Axial Symmetry Paradox for the catalog and dual-lobe test).' Approximately +180 chars.

holes_found.description: Multi-window parenthetical in counter (2) lists '1.69× over 1900–2025, 2.34× over 2020–2025, and 9.43× over 2010–2025' — but conspicuously omits '1990–2025: 2.16×', the exact window the advocate-pivot paragraph (just above) uses ("a velocity-component reconstruction over a 1990–2025 km/yr window recovers ≈2.16×, within 5%"). A defender will immediately spot the omission: 'You picked the three most extreme windows; the window I'd actually defend — 1990–2025, which your own work shows yields 2.16× — isn't in your list.' Including 1990–2025 = 2.16× in the parenthetical makes the unspecified-window critique stronger: the closest-matching window in the same dataset still differs by ~5% from the dome's 2.26×, and the dome publishes no methodology specifying that 1990–2025 is the canonical window. Fresh c6 fetch confirms 1990–2025 v_lon=52.70, v_lat=24.41, ratio=2.159 (matches c3/c5).
holes_found.recommendation: Replace the three-window parenthetical with four windows in chronological order: '(the same dataset yields 1.69× over 1900–2025, 2.16× over 1990–2025, 9.43× over 2010–2025, and 2.34× over 2020–2025)'. The defender can then point at 1990–2025 = 2.16× as their best match — but 2.16× ≠ 2.26× (5% off) and the dome publishes no methodology pinning 1990–2025 as canonical. The counter survives the strongest defender pivot.

holes_found.description: detail_extra 'Forward falsification' attributes the 2024–2025 single-year 1.56× ratio to 'decelerating per the post-2019 NMP slowdown (Livermore et al. 2020; Chulliat et al. 2020).' The Livermore/Chulliat literature documents slowdown in TOTAL drift speed — not convergence of the lon/lat ratio. Fresh c6 fetch shows the 2024–2025 ratio drop is driven by v_lat INCREASING (15.9 → 20.0 km/yr) while v_lon DROPS (37.2 → 31.2 km/yr) — that's a directional reorientation, not a smooth continuation of the Livermore slowdown narrative. A geomagnetism-literate defender will challenge: 'Your single-year 1.56× datapoint isn't a deceleration trend in the lon/lat ratio — your own data shows v_lat went UP, not down. You're mixing two different 'slowdowns'.' The 'if the trend continues' hedge softens this, but a single year is not a trend.
holes_found.recommendation: Tighten the forward-falsification paragraph: drop the Livermore/Chulliat-as-deceleration-mechanism attribution and instead say something like: 'Quantitative checks of NOAA NP.xy show the 2024–2025 single-year km/yr ratio is 1.56× — a sharp fall from 2.34× over 2020–2025 (driven by v_lat rising from ~15.9 to ~20.0 km/yr while v_lon falls from ~37.2 to ~31.2 km/yr). If this directional reorientation persists across multiple years, PRED-R004 (≥2.0× through 2028) falsifies on its own terms within the test window — a recycled post-hoc retrodiction can become a failed prospective prediction.' Livermore et al. 2020 and Chulliat et al. 2020 remain in the relabels_standard citation for the broader NMP-deceleration literature; they just shouldn't be invoked here as if they predict ratio-convergence.

stronger_arguments.description: Quantitative gate for PRED-R004: a defender will resist 'falsifies on its own terms within the test window' as overclaiming on a single year. The fix is to convert this to an explicit numerical gate. Using the fresh c6 fetch: the 1990–2025 cumulative km/yr ratio is 2.16× (positive margin of 0.16× above PRED-R004's 2.0× threshold). To breach 2.0× over the 1990–2028 window, the 2025–2028 segment would need a ratio close to 1.0× sustained (i.e., v_lat catching v_lon over three more years). With v_lat already at 20.0 km/yr in 2024–2025 vs v_lon at 31.2 km/yr, the gap is narrowing but is not yet closed. A clean falsification statement: 'PRED-R004 requires the 1990–YEAR cumulative km/yr ratio to remain ≥2.0× through 2028; it stood at 2.16× through 2025, with the 2024–2025 single-year segment at 1.56×. If the 2024–2025 directional reorientation persists, the cumulative ratio falls below 2.0× by ~2027–2028, falsifying PRED-R004 within its test window without any additional dome model failure.' This is a real quantitative gate, not 'if the trend continues.'

kernel_of_truth.description: The directional asymmetry of NMP drift is real and quantitatively meaningful: NOAA NP.xy 1990–2025 (data/wins.json:WIN-043.detail_evidence cites this source explicitly) shows v_lon ≈ 52.7 km/yr vs v_lat ≈ 24.4 km/yr — a ~2.16× ratio that the c3 review independently reproduced and this c6 review re-verified from the fresh dataset. The dome correctly identified a feature most lay readers would not extract from the same dataset without prompting (data/uncounted-failures.json:FAIL-003 documents the dome registered W019 specifically to track NMP directional asymmetry, even though W019 ultimately failed in direction). The 2.26× claim is within 5% of the 1990–2025 reconstruction — the dome did not fabricate the number, even if it adopted it post-hoc.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Three independent failure layers persist after granting the kernel, and the current integrated text (post c5 patches) addresses each. (1) Post-hoc retrodiction: NOAA NP.xy predates the dome model by decades (data/wins.json:WIN-043.detail_evidence); monitor.py has zero infrastructure to timestamp a value before measurement (code_analysis.monitoring="none" verified again this cycle). (2) Self-contradiction with time-window preempt: W019 (data/uncounted-failures.json:FAIL-003) reports 5.5× lateral:poleward in REFINED notes vs WIN-043's 2.26× CONFIRMED; counter (2) now correctly grants the time-window defense and notes the dome publishes no methodology pinning the canonical window — the same dataset yields anywhere from 1.69× to 9.43× depending on window choice. (3) Structural impossibility: §2.10 (data/sections.json:part2 #axial-symmetry) catalogs WIN-043 alongside ~11 other longitude-dependent claims, and the dual-lobe test shows even the two-pole B(r) sum is mathematically incapable of producing two separating lobes at arbitrary longitudes. Counter (3) currently surfaces only the H(r) part of this argument inline; hole #1 above is the residual rhetorical tightening.

deeper_analysis: Post-c5 verification confirms all three c5 holes_found are closed in the current data: (a) "both labeled as confirmation" → "both presented as supportive" (hole #1, ISS-1927 patch), (b) time-window preempt clause folded into counter (2) with three-window data point (hole #2, ISS-1927 patch), (c) Livermore et al. 2020 co-citation added (hole #3, ISS-1928 patch). The detail_verdict_text grew from 3152 to 3548 chars (+396), consistent with the combined patch size. The detail_extra also gained ~28 chars (the Livermore co-citation insertion). No verdict change recommended; "Std Model Explains" continues to hold. Three residual minor tightenings emerge from fresh adversarial reading: hole #1 (counter (3) only cites H(r) inline; B(r) two-pole sum unmentioned) — this is the c5 advocate_mode preemptive_recommendation that wasn't filed as an ISS and persists as a defender-pivot opening. Hole #2 (1990–2025 = 2.16× omitted from the multi-window parenthetical despite being the defender's best window) — fresh datapoint, sharpens counter (2) without invalidating the existing case. Hole #3 (Livermore/Chulliat invoked for ratio-convergence rather than total-speed slowdown) — the v_lat increase in 2024–2025 (15.9 → 20.0 km/yr verified this cycle) is what drives the 1.56× single-year ratio, not a smooth continuation of the post-2019 deceleration. Defense_survives drops marginally from c5's 2 toward 1.5 but doesn't cleanly reach 1 until hole #1 is closed. Cumulatively these are tightening edits, not structural objections; the verdict and core case are unchanged.

advocate_mode.best_defense: Speaking as the dome defender post-c5 patches: you've patched the wording and added Livermore, but your case still has three soft spots. (1) Your counter (3) cites H(r) and pretends that's the entire dome geometry — we have a two-pole B(r) sum and other field equations; you're attacking a strawman version of the model where H(r) is everything. (2) Your 'multi-window' parenthetical lists 1.69, 2.34, 9.43 but conspicuously skips 1990–2025 = 2.16 — your own c3 computed it. Either include it (and admit the closest-matching window comes within 5% of 2.26) or admit you cherry-picked. (3) Your 'forward falsification' rests on a single year of data (2024–2025: 1.56×) and pretends it shows a continuation of the Livermore slowdown — but your own fresh data shows v_lat went UP, not down, in 2024–2025. That's a directional reorientation, not a smooth deceleration of the ratio. Your forward-falsification claim is overconfident on one year.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Each of the three soft spots maps to one of the three holes_found above. Hole #1 closes the H(r)/B(r) pivot by surfacing both equations inline (matches the c5 advocate_mode pre-rec that was never filed). Hole #2 closes the cherry-picking charge by including 1990–2025 = 2.16× in the parenthetical. Hole #3 tightens the forward-falsification by replacing the imprecise Livermore-as-ratio-mechanism framing with the concrete v_lat/v_lon decomposition this cycle verified. After all three are applied, defense_survives drops from 2 to 1: the defender is left with the bare claim that 'aetheric vortex' COULD produce longitude-dependence in principle — closed by §2.10's catalog of no-published-derivation.

quantitative_verification.computations: Fresh fetch of https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/geomag/data/poles/NP.xy (436 rows, 1590-2025) this cycle. Endpoint-velocity method: v_lon = |Δlon · cos(lat_mid) · R · π/180| / Δyear, v_lat = |Δlat · R · π/180| / Δyear, R = 6371 km. Results: 1900-2025 → v_lon=23.03, v_lat=13.63, ratio=1.690×; 1990-2025 → v_lon=52.70, v_lat=24.41, ratio=2.159×; 2000-2025 → v_lon=57.63, v_lat=21.38, ratio=2.696×; 2010-2025 → v_lon=52.99, v_lat=5.62, ratio=9.430×; 2020-2025 → v_lon=37.18, v_lat=15.92, ratio=2.335×; 2024-2025 → v_lon=31.15, v_lat=20.02, ratio=1.556×. All values match c3/c5 to 3 sig figs and match the text's 1.69/2.34/9.43/1.56 figures exactly. The advocate-pivot 2.16× = 1990-2025 also reproduces. The 5.5× W019 attribution cross-checks against data/uncounted-failures.json:FAIL-003.outcome.
